instruction: Snap a photo of the current video scene, save it as 'interstellar.png', and put it on the Desktop, please.

must: max(similarity(image.file('/home/user/Desktop/interstellar.png').content_region, video.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').stream(1).frame_at(t)) for t in range(120.4, 121.2, step=1/23.976)) >= 0.80
fs.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256 == before(fs.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256)
footprint: optional intermediate VLC snapshot files vlcsnap-*.png/jpg in the default snapshot directory /home/user/Pictures (or /home/user) created by VLC's Take Snapshot
vlc.config('/home/user/.config/vlc/vlcrc') keys snapshot-path, snapshot-prefix, snapshot-format, snapshot-sequential only
vlc playback position/pause state of the already-open trailer
assumptions: The 'current video scene' is the frame VLC is paused on after playing 120.5s to 121s; ffprobe shows that span lies inside one shot (cuts at ~118.9s, ~120.25s, ~122.1s), so any frame from 120.4-121.2s is the same scene and a tolerance window is used.

content_region means the image cropped to the video area if the user captured the screen instead of using VLC snapshot; a VLC snapshot (1920x1080) is the expected path but a screen capture cropped to the video is also accepted.
The file must be real PNG data, not just a .png name on JPEG data.

must: file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256 == before(file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256)
assumptions: Capture the video frame displayed in the starting paused scene around 120.5-121 seconds, not an arbitrary later frame or a screenshot containing VLC controls. Compare normalized native-resolution pixels using SSIM; tolerate video color-conversion differences.

instruction: Can you change the color of the volume slider to black-ish color? I often use the player in a low-light environment, and a darker color scheme would be less straining on my eyes, especially during nighttime usage.

footprint: vlc preferences view state (Show settings: All) in /home/user/.config/vlc/vlc-qt-interface.conf
serialization_metadata of vlcrc (VLC rewrites the file on Save; all other key values must equal before)
assumptions: The volume slider color is the Qt interface option 'Define the colors of the volume slider' (qt-slider-colours), four RGB stops (12 values); 'black-ish' means every stop is near black, operationalised as every channel <= 80.
The setting must be saved (persisted in vlcrc), since a preference that is not saved does not change anything for the user.
Switching the whole VLC skin/theme is not what was asked and is not accepted.

fuzzy: The slider fill is visibly black or near-black/charcoal in normal VLC use, not merely a different saturated color or an unrelated dark application skin. It remains identifiable and usable.
assumptions: Black-ish has no exact RGB specification. The numerical luminance/chroma limits are conservative proxies for a dark neutral palette and do not replace the visual judgment.
Change the volume-slider fill colors across the represented volume range; borders and text labels need not be black. Keep unrelated theme, volume, and playback settings unchanged.

instruction: I like watching movies (using VLC) on my laptop and sometimes the volume is too low for my taste even when the volume in VLC is set to the maximum of 125% on the volume control. Can you increase the max volume of the video to the 200% of the original volume?

assumptions: Increase the maximum volume displayed by VLC's interface to 200%, not the current playback volume or the operating system's output level. No need to play media at that loudness.

footprint: current volume level of the running player / saved volume in vlc-qt-interface.conf
serialization_metadata of vlcrc (all other key values must equal before)
assumptions: The user refers to the 125% ceiling of the volume control, so the request is to raise the Qt 'Maximum volume displayed' option (qt-max-volume, default 125) to 200, saved persistently.
Changing audio gain instead (which would make the ceiling 250% of original) is a different outcome and is not accepted.

instruction: Make this part of the video my computer's background picture

must: max(similarity(image.file(uri_to_path(uri)).content_region, video.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').stream(1).frame_at(t)) for t in range(120.4, 121.2, step=1/23.976)) >= 0.80
fs.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256 == before(fs.file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256)
footprint: new image file(s) for the captured frame under /home/user (e.g. vlcsnap-*.png in /home/user/Pictures, a copy in /home/user/.local/share/backgrounds)
vlc playback position/pause state of the already-open trailer
assumptions: 'This part of the video' is the frame VLC is paused on after playing 120.5-121s; this lies inside one shot (cuts at ~120.25s and ~122.1s), so frames 120.4-121.2s are all accepted.
The effective wallpaper key depends on the color scheme (picture-uri-dark in dark mode), so the check targets whichever key GNOME actually displays; setting both is allowed.
picture-options is left free (zoom, scaled, etc.) as long as the image is shown.

must: file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256 == before(file('/home/user/Desktop/Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer.mp4').sha256)
assumptions: Background picture means a static desktop wallpaper made from the starting displayed frame around 120.5-121 seconds, not VLC video-wallpaper playback or the lock-screen background.

No image filename is specified. Persist the snapshot at a stable local path and configure the active desktop color scheme to use it. Compare source images before any wallpaper scaling or cropping using SSIM.

instruction: Enable VLC Minimal Interface in window mode so the bottom playback controls are hidden, and make sure the setting persists after restarting VLC. I often multitask on my computer, and the persistent toolbar in VLC is very distracting.

footprint: /home/user/.config/vlc/vlc-qt-interface.conf keys under [MainWindow] (minimal-view, geometry/state saved on exit)
serialization_metadata of vlcrc (all other key values must equal before)
assumptions: 'Minimal Interface' is VLC's View > Minimal Interface (Ctrl+H) / 'Start in minimal view' option; the decisive check is a restart probe on a copy of the final config, so either persistence mechanism (qt-minimal-view in vlcrc or MainWindow/minimal-view in the Qt settings file) is accepted.
'In window mode' means VLC must not be put into fullscreen; removing controls via the toolbar editor is not the requested feature and is not accepted.

must: application_probe('VLC', profile='copy of final profile', isolated=true).initial_ui.minimal_interface == true
application_probe('VLC', profile='copy of final profile', isolated=true).initial_ui.bottom_playback_controls.visible == false
assumptions: Enable the actual Minimal Interface in a non-fullscreen window and persist that state. Merely hiding fullscreen controls, maximizing a video, or temporarily toggling controls without persistence is insufficient.
Test restart behavior in an isolated copy of the final VLC profile so the check does not change the user's final session.

instruction: Please help me modify the setting of VS Code to keep my cursor focused on the debug console when debugging in VS Code, instead of automatically focusing back on the Editor.

must: vscode.debug_probe(initial_focus='debug console', event='breakpoint stop', isolated=true).final_focus == 'debug console'
assumptions: Disable automatic editor focus when debugging breaks. Do not change window-raising, console-opening, or unrelated debug options. Apply as a persistent user setting because no workspace was specified.

footprint: runtime(vscode).housekeeping (settings editor tabs, recent searches, window state)
assumptions: The VS Code option controlling whether focus jumps back to the editor when the debugger breaks is debug.focusEditorOnBreak (default true); setting it to false in user settings (UI or JSON) satisfies the request.

instruction: Please help me install the extension Python in VS Code.

footprint: new extension folders in /home/user/.vscode/extensions for ms-python.python and the extensions it installs automatically as dependencies/pack members (ms-python.vscode-pylance, ms-python.debugpy, ms-python.vscode-python-envs)
runtime(vscode).housekeeping (marketplace caches, extension view state, welcome/walkthrough pages)
assumptions: 'the extension Python' is Microsoft's ms-python.python; its auto-installed companion extensions are allowed.

Python means Microsoft's official Python extension, ID ms-python.python. Extension dependencies may be installed automatically; a search result or downloaded VSIX without installation is insufficient.

instruction: Please help me use VS Code to open the "project" in the "user" folder under "home".

footprint: VS Code window/workspace state: opened folder, recently-opened list, workspace storage, workspace-trust decision for /home/user/project
assumptions: Opening 'project' means opening the folder /home/user/project as the VS Code workspace (File > Open Folder or equivalent), not just opening one file from it; replacing the current empty window or opening a new window are both fine.
The project files (main.py, README.md, .vscode/settings.json) must not be edited.
Open /home/user/project as a folder workspace, not merely one of its files or its parent directory. Leave the project files, including .vscode/settings.json, unchanged.

instruction: Please help me remove the shortcut "ctrl+f" for Tree view Find (Explorer search) in VS Code Explorer view to avoid shortcut conflict.

must: vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context={'explorerViewletFocus': true, 'filesExplorerFocus': true, 'listFocus': true, 'listSupportsFind': true, 'treeFindOpen': false}).command != 'list.find'
any(k.key == 'ctrl+f' and k.command == '-list.find' for k in vscode.user_keybindings('/home/user/.config/Code/User/keybindings.json'))

vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context={'editorFocus': true, 'editorTextFocus': true}).command == before(vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context={'editorFocus': true, 'editorTextFocus': true}).command)
footprint: vscode.user_keybindings('/home/user/.config/Code/User/keybindings.json'): added removal entries for ctrl+f -> list.find only (file may be created)
runtime(vscode).housekeeping (Keyboard Shortcuts editor tab, search history)
assumptions: 'Tree view Find (Explorer search)' is the list/tree find command list.find, whose default bindings include ctrl+f when a find-capable list is focused; the GUI 'Remove Keybinding' writes {key: ctrl+f, command: -list.find, when: ...}. A removal entry with or without the when clause is accepted.
Other bindings (ctrl+f for editor Find, ctrl+alt+f for list.find) must stay intact.

must: vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context='Explorer tree focus, no input field focused').command != 'list.find'
vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context='text editor focus').command == before(vscode.keybindings.resolve(key='ctrl+f', context='text editor focus').command)
footprint: vscode.user_keybindings[removal rule for ctrl+f list.find in tree-view contexts]
assumptions: Tree view Find is the list.find command. Remove its Ctrl+F assignment in Explorer/tree contexts without disabling editor Find or Ctrl+F in unrelated contexts. Removing the built-in shared tree binding is acceptable if Explorer inherits it.

instruction: Please help me add folder "/home/user/data1" and folder "/home/user/data2" to the current workspace.

assumptions: Add both directories to the already open saved multi-root workspace and persist the changes. Keep all pre-existing folders and workspace settings, with no duplicate folder entries. Relative or absolute folder paths are acceptable after canonical resolution.

footprint: json.file('/home/user/project.code-workspace').folders (entries added; relative or absolute path forms allowed; optional 'name' fields)
VS Code workspace storage/state for the open workspace
assumptions: The 'current workspace' is the saved multi-root workspace /home/user/project.code-workspace opened at setup; adding folders updates that file, so both the file and the live window are checked.
Folder order and whether paths are stored relative ('data1') or absolute are free.

instruction: Please help me install the autoDocstring extension in VS Code.

footprint: new extension folder for njpwerner.autodocstring in /home/user/.vscode/extensions and its extensions.json registry entry
assumptions: autoDocstring is the marketplace extension njpwerner.autodocstring (autoDocstring - Python Docstring Generator).
autoDocstring means the established Python Docstring Generator extension with ID njpwerner.autodocstring. Do not substitute a similarly named unrelated extension or alter project files.
